page: Amazon Web Services c7g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton3 processor, specifically utilizing the Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz with no hyperthreading. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates solid performance across general compute and memory operations. The instance achieves a Passmark memory score in the top 25%, supported by a strong uncached write memory bandwidth of 93.97 GB/sec. Single-core and multi-core performance metrics, such as Geekbench scores of 1480.0 and 12798.0 respectively, fall within the average range. Cryptographic performance is a relative bottleneck, with the Passmark CPU encryption test registering in the bottom 25% at 2226.35. For language model workloads, the instance handles small 135M models with average efficiency, but struggles on prompt processing for medium 7B models, which falls into the bottom 25% at 28.19 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides a resource-dense alternative to traditional x86 platforms, delivering competitive memory bandwidth and integer processing per unit of resource. Given the lack of local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance is best suited for compute-bound workloads that can leverage multi-core ARM architectures. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, static web serving, Redis in-memory database operations, and lightweight machine learning inference.
